However, the discontinuity between administrations (each new government tends to adopt new plans) has undermined long-term planning. The NDPC coordinates across all government ministries.
laws.penalty: N/A — planning body
exceptions: Annual budgets are the primary binding fiscal instrument
Individual ministries retain significant discretion
laws.source: Ghana Constitution, 1992, Chapter 14; National Development Planning Commission Act

quiz.q: What challenge undermines Ghana's long-term national development planning?
options: Discontinuity as each new government adopts new plans
quiz.explanation: A key challenge for Ghana's NDPC is that each new government tends to adopt its own development plans, creating discontinuity in long-term planning and undermining the consistent implementation needed for transformative development.

laws.title: Securities Law — Menzgold Scandal
laws.subtitle: Capital markets regulation and investor protection
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regulates capital markets under the Securities Industry Act. The Menzgold scandal (2018-2019) exposed regulatory failures when thousands of Ghanaians lost savings in an unlicensed gold trading scheme that operated without SEC approval. The collapse of multiple savings and loans companies (Beige Bank, etc.) in 2017-2019 also highlighted supervisory weaknesses. Bank of Ghana and SEC have since tightened oversight.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for operating unlicensed securities businesses; investor fraud prosecuted
exceptions: Bank-linked investment products regulated by Bank of Ghana
Government securities exempt from SEC requirements

quiz.q: What scandal exposed regulatory failures in Ghana's financial sector around 2018-2019?
options: Menzgold — an unlicensed gold trading scheme where thousands lost savings
quiz.explanation: The Menzgold scandal exposed Ghana's regulatory failures when thousands of Ghanaians lost savings in an unlicensed gold trading scheme operated by Menzgold Ghana Limited without SEC approval, highlighting gaps in securities oversight.

laws.title: Disability Inclusion in Education
laws.subtitle: Special educational needs and inclusive education
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Persons with Disability Act and Education Act require inclusive education for children with disabilities. The Ghana Education Service has a Special Education Division. In practice, inclusive education is limited, with most children with disabilities in urban areas attending special schools rather than mainstream schools. Rural children with disabilities face even greater barriers. The University for Development Studies and other institutions have worked on inclusive education research.
laws.penalty: Administrative sanctions for educational institutions that discriminate against disabled students
exceptions: Severe disabilities may require specialized residential facilities
Private schools have some flexibility in admission criteria
laws.source: Ghana Persons with Disability Act, 2006 (Act 715); Education Act, 2008

quiz.q: What government body implements special education for children with disabilities in Ghana?
options: National Council on Persons with Disabilities
Ghana Education Service Special Education Division
quiz.explanation: The Ghana Education Service's Special Education Division implements special education programs for children with disabilities, though in practice true inclusive education in mainstream schools remains limited.

laws.title: Offshore Oil Regulation — Petroleum Commission
laws.subtitle: Regulation of Ghana's offshore petroleum industry
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Petroleum Commission Act (2011) established the Petroleum Commission to regulate upstream petroleum activities. Ghana's offshore oilfields (Jubilee, TEN, Sankofa-Gye Nyame) are operated by international oil companies including Tullow Oil and Eni. The government holds equity through Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC). Environmental regulation of offshore operations has been a concern, including a 2023 oil spill from the Jubilee Field. Local content requirements mandate Ghanaian participation in the oil industry.
laws.penalty: Fines and license revocation for petroleum regulation violations
exceptions: Force majeure events handled separately
Emergency environmental response protocols override normal procedures

quiz.q: Which international oil companies operate Ghana's major offshore oilfields?
quiz.explanation: Ghana's major offshore oilfields including the Jubilee and TEN fields are operated primarily by Tullow Oil and Eni, with Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) holding equity interest.

laws.title: Teacher Service Conditions
laws.subtitle: Teachers' rights and education labor relations
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Ghana Education Service Act and collective agreements govern teacher employment. The Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) and the Coalition of Concerned Teachers advocate for teacher rights. Teacher strikes have periodically disrupted education, particularly over salary conditions and school infrastructure. Ghana has a shortage of qualified teachers, particularly in northern regions and STEM subjects. The Teacher Licensure Examination was introduced to improve professional standards.
laws.penalty: Disciplinary action for teacher misconduct; criminal charges for sexual abuse of students
exceptions: Private school teachers have different contractual arrangements
International school teachers governed by separate agreements

quiz.q: What was introduced to improve teaching professional standards in Ghana?
quiz.explanation: Ghana introduced the Teacher Licensure Examination to improve professional teaching standards, requiring teachers to pass a licensure exam to practice, addressing concerns about the quality of teacher preparation.

laws.title: Science and Technology Policy
laws.subtitle: Innovation and technology development framework
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's science and technology policy encourages innovation and research. The Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) oversees applied research. Ghana has growing tech hubs in Accra ('Silicon Labadi') and a developing startup ecosystem. The Accra Digital Centre and various incubators support technology entrepreneurship. Ghana has made progress in e-government services including Ghana.gov portal. Brain drain of skilled Ghanaians remains a challenge for building local scientific capacity.
laws.penalty: N/A — science and technology development policy
exceptions: Intellectual property from publicly funded research governed by specific IP policies
Technology transfer agreements with international partners
laws.source: Ghana Science, Technology and Innovation Policy 2017

quiz.q: What nickname has been given to Accra's emerging technology hub?
quiz.explanation: Accra's growing technology and startup ecosystem has been nicknamed 'Silicon Labadi' (referencing Labadi Beach), reflecting Ghana's emergence as a West African technology hub with growing investment in digital innovation.

laws.title: Political Parties Act — Party Funding
laws.subtitle: Regulation of political party financing
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Political Parties Act (2000) regulates political party registration and operations. The act requires parties to be national in character (not regional or ethnic). Political party financing is partially regulated, with some public funding through the Electoral Commission. Campaign finance regulation is weak, with significant concerns about money politics and vote buying. The two dominant parties (NDC and NPP) have dominated Ghanaian politics since 1992, though smaller parties participate.
laws.penalty: Deregistration for parties that violate the Act's requirements
exceptions: Religious and ethnic groups cannot form political parties
Party internal rules are self-regulated with limited external oversight

quiz.q: What requirement does Ghana's Political Parties Act impose on party character?
options: Parties must have at least 50,000 members
Parties must be national in character, not regional or ethnic
Parties must field candidates in all 261 districts
quiz.explanation: Ghana's Political Parties Act requires all registered parties to be national in character, prohibiting regional or ethnic-based parties, reflecting the constitution's effort to prevent ethnically divisive politics.

laws.title: Electronic Transactions Act
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for e-commerce and digital contracts
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Electronic Transactions Act (2008) gives legal recognition to electronic contracts, digital signatures, and electronic records. The act facilitated the growth of e-commerce and digital government services in Ghana. Online consumer protection provisions apply to e-commerce transactions. The act was an important foundation for Ghana's digital economy. Ghana has one of West Africa's most developed e-commerce sectors, though consumer protection enforcement online remains limited.
laws.penalty: Civil liability for electronic contract breaches; criminal penalties for electronic fraud
exceptions: Certain transactions still require paper (e.g., real property transfers)
Government processes may require original documents in some cases

quiz.q: What did Ghana's Electronic Transactions Act give legal recognition to?
options: Electronic contracts, digital signatures, and electronic records
quiz.explanation: Ghana's Electronic Transactions Act (2008) gave legal recognition to electronic contracts, digital signatures, and electronic records, providing the legal foundation for Ghana's growing e-commerce sector and digital government services.

laws.title: Green Building and Urban Sustainability
laws.subtitle: Building regulations with environmental standards
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's building regulations have been updated to include energy efficiency requirements. The Energy Commission has promoted solar energy for homes and businesses. The Greater Accra Metropolitan Area faces severe air pollution from vehicular traffic and industrial activities. Waste management in Accra and other cities is a major environmental challenge. Illegal dumping is widespread. The government has pursued public-private partnerships for waste management, including Zoomlion Ghana.
laws.penalty: Fines for building code violations and illegal dumping
exceptions: Rural buildings exempt from many urban building codes
Traditional construction materials may have exemptions
laws.source: Ghana Building Regulations, 1996 (LI 1630); Energy Commission Act

quiz.q: What is a major environmental challenge facing Accra and other Ghanaian cities?
options: Severe air pollution and inadequate waste management
quiz.explanation: Accra faces severe air pollution from vehicular traffic and industrial activities, combined with major waste management challenges including illegal dumping and inadequate waste collection infrastructure.

laws.title: Child Rights — Birth Registration
laws.subtitle: Universal birth registration and documentation
laws.fullDescription: Ghana has worked to improve birth registration rates as part of children's rights. The Births and Deaths Registry, under the Vital Registration Act, registers births and deaths. Low birth registration rates in rural areas have denied children access to education and health services. Ghana has introduced community-level registration to improve coverage. National identification (the Ghana Card) is linked to birth registration. Unregistered children face difficulties accessing services and proving citizenship.
laws.penalty: N/A — civil registration administrative framework
exceptions: Late registration procedures for previously unregistered individuals
Mobile registration for remote communities
laws.source: Ghana Vital Registration Act; Births and Deaths Registry

quiz.q: What key service is the Ghana Card (national ID) linked to?
quiz.explanation: Ghana's national identification system (the Ghana Card) is linked to birth registration and citizenship documentation, making birth registration critical for children's ability to access services and prove their identity.

laws.title: Anti-Corruption in Public Procurement
laws.subtitle: Corruption in government contracting
laws.fullDescription: Corruption in public procurement is a major problem in Ghana, with procurement fraud in infrastructure projects estimated to cost hundreds of millions of dollars annually. The Public Procurement Authority (PPA) oversees implementation of procurement laws and has the power to investigate violations. Common violations include inflated contract prices, single-sourcing without justification, payment for non-performed work, and conflict of interest. The Special Prosecutor's Office has targeted procurement fraud.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment and fines; contract termination and blacklisting of suppliers
exceptions: Emergency procurement procedures allow faster processes
National security procurements have classified procedures
laws.source: Ghana Public Procurement Act, 2003 (Act 663) as amended

quiz.q: What types of procurement violations are most common in Ghana?
options: Inflated contract prices, improper single-sourcing, and payment for non-performed work
quiz.explanation: Common procurement violations in Ghana include inflated contract prices, unjustified single-sourcing, payment for non-performed work, and conflicts of interest, costing hundreds of millions of dollars annually.

laws.title: International Human Rights — Treaty Obligations
laws.subtitle: Ghana's human rights treaty commitments
laws.fullDescription: Ghana has ratified most major international human rights treaties including the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR), Convention Against Torture (CAT), Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC), and African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights. Ghana generally cooperates with UN human rights mechanisms and submits reports. Periodic reviews under the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) have led to some reforms.
laws.penalty: N/A — treaty obligations
exceptions: Some treaty provisions self-executing; others require domestic legislation
Derogations permitted under ICCPR for genuine emergencies
laws.source: Various UN Human Rights Treaties; African Charter
laws.sourceLabel: Ghana's International Human Rights Treaty Obligations

quiz.q: What UN mechanism does Ghana participate in that reviews its human rights record?
quiz.explanation: Ghana participates in the Universal Periodic Review (UPR), a UN mechanism where member states review each other's human rights record, and Ghana has made commitments based on UPR recommendations that have led to some legal reforms.

laws.title: Ghana Stock Exchange
laws.subtitle: Capital market development and regulation
laws.fullDescription: The Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE), established in 1990, is one of Africa's better-performing stock exchanges. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regulates listed companies and market participants. The GSE Composite Index tracks market performance. Major listed companies include Ecobank, MTN Ghana, Tullow Oil, and banks. Despite its development, Ghana's capital market is relatively small and illiquid. The introduction of the Ghana Fixed Income Market (GFIM) has improved bond market infrastructure.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for insider trading, market manipulation, and securities fraud
exceptions: Government securities have different trading rules
Foreign portfolio investors subject to capital flow regulations
laws.source: Ghana Securities Industry Act, 2016 (Act 929); GSE Regulations

quiz.q: When was the Ghana Stock Exchange established?
quiz.explanation: The Ghana Stock Exchange was established in 1990, making it one of Africa's earlier stock exchanges. It lists major Ghanaian companies and has developed into a relatively sophisticated market, though still relatively small by global standards.

laws.title: Forced Labor and Modern Slavery
laws.subtitle: Prohibition of forced labor under domestic and international law
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Labour Act and Criminal Offences Act prohibit forced labor. Ghana has ratified ILO Conventions on forced labor (No. 29 and 105). Despite legal prohibitions, forms of forced labor persist including child labor in fishing (Lake Volta), forced domestic work, and debt bondage in fishing communities. The Labour Department and social welfare services work to identify and assist victims. Ghana participates in US government initiatives to address forced labor including the Trafficking in Persons report.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties including imprisonment for forced labor practices; fines
exceptions: Prison labor subject to separate regulation
National service programs constitute compelled service but are legally permitted
laws.source: Ghana Labour Act, 2003; Criminal Offences Act; ILO Conventions

quiz.q: What international labor standards has Ghana ratified regarding forced labor?
options: African Union Convention on Labor Rights
quiz.explanation: Ghana has ratified ILO Conventions No. 29 (Forced Labour Convention, 1930) and No. 105 (Abolition of Forced Labour Convention, 1957), though forced labor in various forms including child fishing labor on Lake Volta persists.

laws.title: Microfinance and Savings — Rural Finance
laws.subtitle: Susu savings groups and rural credit
laws.fullDescription: Ghana has a rich tradition of informal savings groups called 'susu' where members make regular contributions to a pool, with each member taking turns receiving the accumulated fund. The Susu Collectors Association regulates some informal operators. Formal microfinance institutions are regulated by the Bank of Ghana. The collapse of multiple microfinance companies in 2019 (linked to the broader financial sector cleanup) cost depositors significantly. Rural and Agricultural Finance Institution (RAFIN) supports agricultural lending.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for fraud in licensed microfinance; deposit protection limited
exceptions: Informal susu groups largely unregulated
Cooperative credit unions under separate regulatory framework
laws.source: Ghana Microfinance and Small Loans Centre; Bank of Ghana MFI Guidelines

quiz.q: What is a 'susu' in the context of Ghanaian financial practices?
options: An informal rotating savings group where members contribute to a pool
quiz.explanation: A 'susu' is a traditional Ghanaian informal rotating savings group (similar to 'tontine' in West Africa) where members make regular contributions to a pool, with each member taking turns receiving the accumulated fund.

laws.title: Emergency Powers and Disaster Management
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for emergency response
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) Act governs disaster preparedness and response. The government can declare states of emergency under the constitution for natural disasters, public health emergencies, or security situations. During the COVID-19 pandemic, President Akufo-Addo declared a partial lockdown under the Imposition of Restrictions Act (2020). Ghana's emergency management system has been tested by floods, droughts, and disease outbreaks. Disaster risk reduction is integrated into development planning.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for obstruction of disaster management operations
exceptions: Emergency declarations suspend normal procurement requirements
Military and security forces have enhanced powers during emergencies
laws.source: Ghana NADMO Act, 1996 (Act 517); Imposition of Restrictions Act, 2020

quiz.q: Under what law did Ghana implement COVID-19 lockdowns?
quiz.explanation: Ghana implemented its COVID-19 lockdowns under the Imposition of Restrictions Act (2020), legislation passed specifically to allow the President to impose restrictions on movement and gatherings during public health emergencies.

laws.title: Traditional Medicine and Herbal Industry
laws.subtitle: Regulation of herbal medicines and traditional healers
laws.fullDescription: Ghana has a significant traditional medicine sector with thousands of traditional healers and herbal medicine practitioners. The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) regulates herbal medicines as products, requiring registration and safety testing. The Traditional Medicine Practice Council regulates practitioners. Herbal medicines are widely used alongside conventional medicine. Some herbal products from Ghana (shea butter, neem) have been successfully commercialized internationally. The integration of traditional medicine into the healthcare system is a national policy goal.
laws.penalty: FDA fines for unregistered herbal products; criminal penalties for harmful traditional practices
exceptions: Traditional healers can practice within regulated framework
Herbal gardens on licensed premises may operate
laws.source: Ghana Traditional Medicine Practice Council Act, 2000 (Act 575)

quiz.q: Which body regulates traditional medicine practitioners in Ghana?
quiz.explanation: The Traditional Medicine Practice Council, established under the 2000 Act, regulates traditional medicine practitioners in Ghana, while the FDA separately regulates herbal medicine products for safety and quality.

laws.title: Port and Harbour Regulation
laws.subtitle: Tema and Takoradi ports governance
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's major ports at Tema (near Accra) and Takoradi are managed by Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) under the Ports and Harbours Act. Tema Port is West Africa's largest container port. The ports are critical for Ghana's landlocked neighbors including Burkina Faso, Niger, and Mali. Port efficiency has been a concern, with cargo clearance times exceeding regional benchmarks. Ghana has signed concession agreements with DP World for the Tema Container Terminal.
laws.penalty: Fines for customs violations; criminal penalties for smuggling
exceptions: Free zones operators at ports have streamlined procedures
Diplomatic goods exempt from most inspections
laws.source: Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority Act, 1986 (PNDCL 160)

quiz.q: Which West African landlocked countries rely heavily on Ghana's ports for their international trade?
quiz.explanation: Ghana's Tema and Takoradi ports are critical trade gateways for landlocked neighbors including Burkina Faso, Niger, and Mali, making Ghana's port efficiency of regional economic significance.

laws.title: National Commission for Civic Education
laws.subtitle: Civic education for democratic participation
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) is a constitutional body established to educate citizens about their rights, responsibilities, and the workings of government. The NCCE conducts community education programs, particularly around election times. The commission is considered an important institution supporting Ghana's democratic culture. It works to promote the values of the 1992 Constitution and ensure citizens can participate meaningfully in governance.
laws.penalty: N/A — educational body
exceptions: Partisan political content excluded from NCCE programming
External organizations can conduct civic education independently
laws.sourceLabel: National Commission for Civic Education Act

quiz.q: What is the primary role of Ghana's National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE)?
options: Educate citizens about their rights, responsibilities, and democratic governance
quiz.explanation: The NCCE is a constitutional body that educates citizens about their rights, responsibilities, and government, supporting Ghana's democratic culture by ensuring citizens can participate meaningfully in governance processes.

laws.title: Sexual Offenses Against Children
laws.subtitle: Child sexual abuse and exploitation laws
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Criminal Offences Act, Children's Act, and Human Trafficking Act provide protections against sexual abuse of children. Defilement (sexual intercourse with a child under 16) carries heavy penalties. Child sexual exploitation and grooming are criminalized. Online child sexual abuse material (CSAM) is criminalized under the Cybersecurity Act. Despite legal protections, reporting rates for child sexual abuse are very low due to stigma, lack of awareness, and perpetrators often being family members or trusted individuals.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment 7-25 years for defilement; life imprisonment for aggravated cases involving violence
exceptions: Mandatory reporting by medical professionals and teachers
Victim identity protected in court proceedings
laws.source: Ghana Criminal Offences Act, Section 101; Children's Act, 1998 (Act 560)

quiz.q: What is the minimum age of a child victim that constitutes 'defilement' under Ghana's Criminal Offences Act?
quiz.explanation: Under Ghana's Criminal Offences Act, 'defilement' refers to sexual intercourse with a child under 16 years of age, regardless of consent, and carries imprisonment sentences of 7-25 years.

laws.title: Foreign Policy — Pan-Africanism
laws.subtitle: Ghana's pan-African identity and international role
laws.fullDescription: Ghana, under its first President Kwame Nkrumah, was a founding voice for pan-Africanism and African unity. Ghana was a founding member of the Organisation of African Unity (now African Union) in 1963. Ghana has contributed troops to numerous UN peacekeeping missions. Ghana hosts several international organizations including the ECOWAS Court of Justice and various UN agencies. Ghana has generally maintained a pro-Western foreign policy while also engaging with China, Russia, and emerging powers.
laws.penalty: N/A — foreign policy framework
exceptions: Treaty obligations prevail over ordinary domestic law
Security Council resolutions binding under international law
laws.source: Ghana Constitution, Article 40; Foreign Policy documents

quiz.q: Who was Ghana's first President and a leading voice for pan-Africanism?
quiz.explanation: Kwame Nkrumah was Ghana's first President (1957-1966) and a towering figure in pan-Africanism, advocating for African unity, and playing a key role in founding the Organisation of African Unity (now the African Union).

laws.title: Renewable Energy Policy
laws.subtitle: Solar and renewable energy development framework
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Renewable Energy Act (2011) established a framework for developing renewable energy sources including solar, wind, hydroelectric, and biomass. The Ghana Energy Commission manages renewable energy licensing. Ghana has significant solar energy potential (average 5.5 peak sun hours/day). Several solar projects have been developed, but renewable energy still constitutes a small percentage of total generation. Net metering regulations allow household solar installations to sell electricity back to the grid.
laws.penalty: License violations subject to fines
exceptions: Off-grid rural electrification projects have simplified licensing
Small household solar installations may not require full licensing

quiz.q: What does Ghana's net metering regulation allow household solar owners to do?
options: Sell excess electricity back to the grid
quiz.explanation: Ghana's net metering regulations allow households with solar installations to sell excess electricity back to the national grid, providing an incentive for household solar adoption and contributing to renewable energy goals.

laws.title: Maternal and Child Health Law
laws.subtitle: Legal protections for maternal and child health
laws.fullDescription: Ghana has made significant progress in reducing maternal and infant mortality through policies including skilled birth attendance, antenatal care, and community health workers (Community Health Planning and Services — CHPS). The NHIS covers maternal healthcare including antenatal care, delivery, and postnatal care. Ghana has trained and deployed thousands of community health officers. Traditional birth attendants (TBAs) are regulated and integrated into the health system. Teenage pregnancy remains a challenge.
laws.penalty: Healthcare providers face regulatory sanctions for below-standard maternal care
exceptions: Emergency obstetric care must be provided regardless of ability to pay
Community health workers have limited scope of practice protections
laws.source: Ghana Maternal Health Policy; NHIS Act, 2003

quiz.q: What primary health strategy has Ghana deployed to reach rural communities for maternal and child health?
options: Community Health Planning and Services (CHPS) with community health workers
quiz.explanation: Ghana's Community Health Planning and Services (CHPS) strategy deploys community health officers in rural communities as frontline health workers for maternal and child health, a model that has significantly improved health access in remote areas.

laws.title: Women in Agriculture — Land Rights
laws.subtitle: Gender gaps in agricultural land access
laws.fullDescription: Despite women making up the majority of Ghana's agricultural workforce (estimates suggest 60-70% of food farmers are women), women have significantly less access to land ownership and credit than men. Customary inheritance practices in many Ghanaian communities favor male heirs. The Land Act (2020) includes some gender-equity provisions in land administration, but customary norms remain dominant. Programs by NGOs and government agencies have worked to improve women's land security.
laws.penalty: Anti-discrimination laws apply in principle; customary violations rarely prosecuted
exceptions: Matrilineal communities (e.g., Akan) have different inheritance norms that may favor women
Legal advocacy organizations work on customary land rights for women
laws.source: Ghana Land Act, 2020; Women's Land Rights Advocacy

quiz.q: What percentage of Ghana's food farmers are estimated to be women?
quiz.explanation: Despite making up an estimated 60-70% of Ghana's food farmers, women have significantly less access to land ownership and agricultural credit than men, with customary inheritance practices often favoring male heirs.

laws.title: Serious Fraud Office
laws.subtitle: Investigation of serious financial crimes
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Serious Fraud Office (SFO, now operating under EOCO for some functions) was established to investigate and prosecute complex fraud cases. The SFO has handled cases involving bank fraud, Ponzi schemes, and government financial misconduct. Ghana's financial sector has experienced significant fraud, including mobile money fraud ('sika gari' scams) and investment fraud. The Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) works alongside fraud investigation bodies to track money flows.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment and fines for serious fraud; asset forfeiture available
exceptions: Minor fraud below threshold handled by regular police
Civil fraud remedies run parallel to criminal prosecutions
laws.source: Ghana Serious Fraud Office Act, 1993; EOCO Act, 2010

quiz.q: What term describes mobile money fraud schemes in Ghana?
quiz.explanation: 'Sika gari' (literally 'money to be burnt') is the local term for various mobile money fraud schemes in Ghana, where fraudsters trick victims into believing they've won prizes or convinced to hand over mobile money.

laws.title: Air Quality and Vehicle Emissions
laws.subtitle: Air pollution control in urban areas
laws.fullDescription: Accra and Kumasi face serious air quality problems from vehicle emissions, construction dust, and open burning. Ghana's EPA has air quality standards, but enforcement is limited. Vehicle emissions testing is part of the roadworthiness certificate requirement but often poorly enforced. The Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) fleet includes many old, high-emission vehicles. Accra consistently ranks among Africa's most polluted cities. Respiratory disease rates are increasing.
laws.penalty: Fines for vehicles failing emissions tests; EPA sanctions for industrial air pollution
exceptions: Emergency generators widely used due to dumsor exempt from some regulations
Traditional burning practices in rural areas treated differently
laws.source: Ghana EPA Act, 1994 (Act 490); Environmental Assessment Regulations

quiz.q: What city consistently ranks among Africa's most polluted due to vehicle emissions and construction dust?
quiz.explanation: Accra, Ghana's capital, consistently ranks among Africa's most polluted cities, with vehicle emissions from a large fleet of aging vehicles, construction dust, and open burning contributing to serious air quality problems.

laws.title: Inheritance Law — Intestate Succession
laws.subtitle: PNDCL 111 — equal inheritance rights
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Intestate Succession Law (PNDCL 111, 1985) significantly reformed inheritance by giving surviving spouses and children equal rights to inherit, overriding customary laws that had often excluded spouses (particularly women) from inheritance. Before PNDCL 111, many widows were dispossessed by the deceased husband's family. Despite the law, enforcement in rural areas where customary practice prevails is weak. The Marriage Act and PNDCL 111 together form the framework for inheritance rights.
laws.penalty: Civil remedies for wrongful deprivation of inheritance; criminal fraud in some cases
exceptions: PNDCL 111 only applies to those without valid wills
Registered customary marriage spouses may have different status

quiz.q: What problem did Ghana's Intestate Succession Law (PNDCL 111) address for widows?
options: Widows being dispossessed by the deceased husband's family under customary law
Disputes between children of different wives
quiz.explanation: PNDCL 111 addressed the widespread practice of widows being dispossessed by their deceased husband's family under customary law, giving surviving spouses equal inheritance rights and providing legal protection for widows.

laws.title: Immigration and Border Control
laws.subtitle: Entry, residence, and deportation law
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Immigration Act (2000) governs entry, residence, and deportation. Ghana is party to ECOWAS free movement protocols, allowing citizens of ECOWAS member states to enter Ghana without a visa for up to 90 days. However, non-ECOWAS foreigners require visas. Ghana has been a destination for immigrants from other African countries, as well as Chinese businesspeople. Anti-Chinese sentiment has arisen over Chinese involvement in illegal galamsey mining. Ghana's Aliens Act imposes restrictions on foreigners working in certain sectors.
laws.penalty: Fines and deportation for immigration violations; criminal penalties for illegal entry
exceptions: ECOWAS citizens have free movement rights
Refugees and asylum seekers have protected status
laws.source: Ghana Immigration Act, 2000 (Act 573); ECOWAS Free Movement Protocol

quiz.q: What right do citizens of ECOWAS member states have when entering Ghana?
options: Visa-free entry for up to 90 days
quiz.explanation: Under ECOWAS free movement protocols, citizens of ECOWAS member states can enter Ghana without a visa for up to 90 days, reflecting the regional integration commitment to free movement of persons.

laws.title: Infrastructure Concessions and PPP Law
laws.subtitle: Public-private partnerships for infrastructure
laws.fullDescription: Ghana has used public-private partnerships (PPPs) for infrastructure development including ports, roads, and utilities. The PPP Policy and Institutional Framework provides guidelines, while specific concession agreements are negotiated for individual projects. The Ghana Concessions Act provides the legislative basis. Notable PPPs include the Tema Container Terminal (DP World) and water sector management. Critics have raised concerns about lack of transparency and fiscal risks from PPP guarantees.
laws.penalty: Contract penalties for PPP non-performance; state can terminate concessions for serious violations
exceptions: PPP agreements supersede general procurement rules in specific areas
Confidentiality provisions in some PPP agreements limit public scrutiny
laws.source: Ghana Concessions Act, 1962 (Act 124); PPP Policy Framework

quiz.q: Which international company operates the Tema Container Terminal under a PPP concession?
quiz.explanation: DP World, the Dubai-based port operator, was awarded a concession to develop and manage the Tema Container Terminal, one of Ghana's major PPP infrastructure deals intended to improve port efficiency.

laws.title: Technical and Vocational Education
laws.subtitle: TVET development for skills training
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) policy aims to develop skills for the labor market. The Council for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (COTVET) oversees TVET. There is a significant skills mismatch in Ghana's labor market — graduates lack practical skills demanded by employers, while TVET is sometimes seen as inferior to university education. The government has promoted TVET as an alternative pathway to university, with mixed results in changing cultural attitudes.
laws.penalty: N/A — educational policy
exceptions: Apprenticeship system operates alongside formal TVET
International certification programs recognized separately

quiz.q: What body oversees Technical and Vocational Education and Training in Ghana?
options: Council for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (COTVET)
quiz.explanation: The Council for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (COTVET), established under the 2006 Act, oversees TVET in Ghana and works to develop vocational skills for the labor market, though skills mismatch and cultural attitudes toward TVET remain challenges.

laws.title: African Continental Free Trade Area
laws.subtitle: Ghana and AfCFTA implementation
laws.fullDescription: Ghana is a strong supporter of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), and Accra is home to the AfCFTA Secretariat. Ghana was among the first countries to ratify AfCFTA. The agreement, which entered into force in 2019, aims to create a single market for goods and services across Africa with 1.4 billion people. Implementation is gradual, with tariff schedules being negotiated. AfCFTA could significantly boost intra-African trade from its current low level of around 15% of total African trade.
laws.penalty: N/A — trade agreement obligations
exceptions: Sensitive goods lists allow protection of some sectors
Rules of origin requirements prevent trade deflection
laws.source: African Continental Free Trade Area Agreement; Ghana AfCFTA Ratification

quiz.q: Where is the AfCFTA Secretariat located?
quiz.explanation: The AfCFTA Secretariat is located in Accra, Ghana, reflecting Ghana's strong support for the African Continental Free Trade Area and its role as a hub for African economic integration.

laws.title: Judicial Corruption — Anas Investigation
laws.subtitle: Anti-corruption in Ghana's judiciary
laws.fullDescription: In 2015, investigative journalist Anas Aremeyaw Anas released footage showing numerous Ghanaian judges accepting bribes in exchange for favorable rulings. The investigation led to the dismissal or disciplinary action against over 30 judges and magistrates, including some High Court judges. The Judicial Council reviewed all cases. The scandal exposed systemic corruption in Ghana's judiciary and prompted reforms. Ghana's courts have generally maintained their institutional independence despite corruption challenges.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution and professional sanction for corrupt judges
exceptions: Judicial immunity does not extend to criminal activity
Whistle-blower protections apply to those exposing judicial corruption

quiz.q: How many judges and magistrates were dismissed or disciplined following the 2015 Anas judicial corruption investigation?
quiz.explanation: Anas Aremeyaw Anas's 2015 undercover investigation led to the dismissal or disciplinary action against over 30 Ghanaian judges and magistrates who were caught on camera accepting bribes for favorable rulings.

laws.title: Freedom of Expression — Online Speech
laws.subtitle: Digital rights and online expression
laws.fullDescription: Ghana's constitutional guarantee of freedom of expression extends to online speech. The 2020 Cybersecurity Act criminalizes 'cyberstalking' and online harassment but has been criticized for potential overreach. There have been cases of journalists and citizens arrested for online speech critical of government officials. The National Communications Authority has the power to direct blocking of websites. Ghana's vibrant social media scene has been a platform for political discourse and civic activism.
laws.penalty: Civil defamation suits; criminal charges for cyberstalking and online harassment
exceptions: Satire and political commentary broadly protected under constitution
Academic and journalistic expression given wide latitude
laws.sourceLabel: Freedom of Expression and Online Speech

quiz.q: What criticism has been raised about Ghana's 2020 Cybersecurity Act?
options: Penalties are too light for serious cybercrime
It does not cover financial cybercrime
'Cyberstalking' and similar provisions could be used to restrict legitimate online speech
It only applies to foreign actors
quiz.explanation: Ghana's 2020 Cybersecurity Act has been criticized because its broad 'cyberstalking' and online harassment provisions could potentially be used to restrict legitimate online speech, criticism of government, or investigative journalism.

laws.title: Volta River Authority
laws.subtitle: Hydroelectric management and water regulation
laws.fullDescription: The Volta River Authority (VRA) was established by the Volta River Development Act (1961) to manage the Akosombo hydroelectric dam and Lake Volta. Akosombo Dam provides the majority of Ghana's electricity. Lake Volta is the world's largest artificial reservoir by surface area. The VRA also manages the Kpong Dam. Lake Volta supports significant fishing and irrigation. Water levels affect electricity generation, and climate change threatens to reduce water availability. The dam's construction displaced approximately 78,000 people.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for unauthorized water abstraction from VRA systems
exceptions: Fishing on Lake Volta regulated separately by Fisheries Commission
Irrigation rights allocated by Water Resources Commission

quiz.q: What unique distinction does Lake Volta hold globally?
options: Largest artificial lake by water volume
Largest artificial reservoir by surface area
quiz.explanation: Lake Volta, created by the Akosombo Dam completed in 1965, is the world's largest artificial reservoir by surface area, covering approximately 8,502 square kilometers and displacing approximately 78,000 people during its creation.

laws.title: Ghana at 67 — Democratic Consolidation
laws.subtitle: Ghana's democratic achievements and ongoing challenges
laws.fullDescription: Ghana celebrated 67 years of independence in 2024. The country has been a model for African democracy with peaceful transfers of power, strong civil society, independent media, and constitutional governance. However, challenges remain: corruption, youth unemployment, infrastructure deficits, health and education gaps, and economic volatility. Ghana's experience offers lessons for African democratic development. The 2024 elections saw another competitive and peaceful contest. Ghana is proof that stable democracy is achievable in Africa.
laws.penalty: N/A — constitutional summary
exceptions: Democratic norms require constant reinforcement
Institutional independence must be actively protected

quiz.q: What year did Ghana become independent and begin its democratic journey?
quiz.explanation: Ghana became independent on March 6, 1957, becoming the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule. Under Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana has since developed into one of Africa's strongest democracies.
